acts.description: Consolidates and amends the provisions relating to criminal offences in India, replacing the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Consolidates and amends the law relating to criminal procedure in India, replacing the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Consolidates and provides general rules and principles of evidence for fair trial, replacing the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
Provides for protection of the interests of consumers and establishes consumer dispute redressal commissions.
Defines and amends the law relating to promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques.
Framework to regulate the renting of premises and to balance the interests of owner and tenant.
Defines the law relating to contracts and agreements in India.

acts.short_title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
acts.description: Provides protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace and for prevention and redressal.
Provides for a scheme for the payment of gratuity to employees engaged in factories, mines, oilfields, and other establishments.

acts.short_title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
acts.description: Provides for more effective protection of the rights of women guaranteed under the Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family.

section.title: Punishment for murder
section.text: (1) Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. (2) When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

corresponds_to.notes: Sub-section (1) corresponds to IPC Section 302. Sub-section (2) introduces a specific penalty for mob lynching/hate murders.

judgments.title: Chherturam @ Chainu vs The State of Chhattisgarh
judgments.ratio_decidendi: When injuries are inflicted on vital body parts in a merciless manner with repeated blows that make survival impossible, the act constitutes murder under Section 302 IPC, and intoxication does not provide a defense under Section 86 IPC.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Punishment for murder - life imprisonment or death penalty with fine

section.title: Cheating
section.text: (1) Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property... commits cheating. (2) Whoever cheats shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both. (4) Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property... shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

corresponds_to.notes: BNS Section 318(4) corresponds directly to Section 420 IPC (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property).
BNS Section 318(1) defines cheating, replacing Section 415 IPC.

judgments.title: Prof. R.K. Vijayasarathy vs Sudha Seetharam
judgments.ratio_decidendi: To establish the offence of cheating under Section 420 IPC (now BNS 318(4)), dishonest intention must be shown to exist at the very time of making the representation or inducement. Mere subsequent breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Ingredients of Cheating - fraudulent or dishonest inducement at the inception

section.title: When police may arrest without warrant
section.text: (1) Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits, in the presence of a police officer, a cognizable offence... Provided that in offences punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years, arrest shall not be made automatically without satisfying conditions of necessity.

corresponds_to.notes: Corresponds to CrPC Section 41 and incorporates Arnesh Kumar guidelines regarding mandatory notice of appearance.

judgments.title: Arnesh Kumar vs State of Bihar
judgments.ratio_decidendi: No arrest should be made automatically in offences punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment. The police officer must satisfy themselves of the necessity of arrest based on the parameters set out in CrPC 41 (now BNSS 35) and record written reasons.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Arrest guidelines - mandatory checklist and reasons before arresting an accused

section.title: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
section.text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid... such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
section.court_triable: Judicial Magistrate of the first class / Metropolitan Magistrate

judgments.title: Dashrathbhai Trikambhai Patel vs Hitesh Mahendrabhai Patel
judgments.ratio_decidendi: For an offence under Section 138 of the NI Act to be made out, the cheque must represent an existing legally enforceable debt or liability on the date of presentation. If part-payment has been made and not endorsed on the cheque under Section 56, the cheque cannot be presented for the full sum.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Dishonour of Cheque - existence of legally enforceable liability at presentation

section.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made
section.text: (1) A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, any recognized consumer association, or the Central Authority. The complaint may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed.

corresponds_to.notes: Replaces Section 12 of the 1986 Act, adding explicit electronic filing rights (e-Daakhil) and jurisdiction based on the complainant's residence.

section.title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
section.text: (1) Every police officer or other person arresting any person without warrant shall forthwith communicate to him full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest. (2) Where a police officer arrests without warrant any person other than a person accused of a non-bailable offence, he shall inform the person arrested that he is entitled to be released on bail and that he may arrange for sureties on his behalf.

corresponds_to.notes: Corresponds to Section 50 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

judgments.title: D.K. Basu vs State of West Bengal
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Arrest without informing grounds of arrest and informing relatives within 8-12 hours violates fundamental rights under Article 21 and 22(1). Mandatory preparation of Arrest Memo required.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Grounds of arrest and communication to friends/family

section.title: Police officer's power to require attendance of witnesses
section.text: (1) Any police officer making an investigation may, by order in writing, require the attendance before himself of any person being within the limits of his own or any adjoining station who, from the information given or otherwise, appears to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case: Provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or of the age of sixty years or above or a woman or a person with disability shall be required to attend at any place other than the place in which such person resides.

judgments.title: Nandini Satpathy vs P.L. Dani
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Article 20(3) right against self-incrimination applies at the stage of police questioning under Section 160 CrPC (now BNSS 179). An accused person cannot be coerced into answering self-incriminating queries.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Police summons and right to silence

section.title: Examination of arrested person by medical officer
section.text: (1) When any person is arrested, he shall be examined by a medical officer in the service of Central Government or a State Government, and in case the medical officer is not available, by a registered medical practitioner, immediately after the arrest is made. (2) The medical officer shall prepare the record of such examination, mentioning therein any injuries or marks of violence upon the person arrested, and the approximate time when such injuries or marks may have been inflicted.

section.title: Person arrested not to be detained more than twenty-four hours
section.text: No police officer shall detain in custody a person arrested without warrant for a longer period than under all the circumstances of the case is reasonable, and such period shall not, in the absence of a special order of a Magistrate under section 187, exceed twenty-four hours exclusive of the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the Magistrate's Court.

corresponds_to.notes: Corresponds to Section 57 CrPC 1973 and Article 22(2) of the Constitution.

judgments.title: Manoj vs State of M.P.
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Detention beyond 24 hours without production before a Magistrate is unlawful and renders the police officers liable for illegal confinement under criminal law.

section.title: Agreement in restraint of trade, void
section.text: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void. Exception 1: One who sells the goodwill of a business may agree with the buyer to refrain from carrying on a similar business, within specified local limits, so long as the buyer carries on a like business therein.

judgments.title: Percept D'Mark (India) Pvt. Ltd. vs Zaheer Khan
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a restrictive covenant extending beyond the term of the agreement is void and unenforceable. The doctrine of restraint of trade does not permit post-contractual non-compete covenants against individuals.

section.title: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
section.text: (1) If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain: (a) his wife, unable to maintain herself, or (b) his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, whether married or not, unable to maintain itself, or (d) his father or mother, unable to maintain himself or herself, a Magistrate of the first class may, upon proof of such neglect or refusal, order such person to make a monthly allowance for the maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother, at such monthly rate as such Magistrate thinks fit.
section.court_triable: Magistrate of the first class / Family Court

judgments.title: Rajnesh vs Neha
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Both parties in all maintenance proceedings under Section 125 CrPC (now BNSS 144), PWDVA, and Hindu Marriage Act must mandatorily file comprehensive Affidavits of Assets and Liabilities. Maintenance awarded must be realistic and commensurate with the standard of living enjoyed in matrimonial home.
judgments.applied_to_this_section: Interim and final maintenance calculation guidelines

section.title: Entry of premises by landlord or property manager
section.text: (1) A landlord or the property manager may enter the premises rented by giving a prior notice of twenty-four hours to the tenant. (2) The entry shall be between nine o'clock in the morning and six o'clock in the evening to carry out inspection or necessary repairs.

section.title: Security deposit refund upon vacation
section.text: The security deposit paid by the tenant shall be refunded to the tenant on the date of taking over vacant possession of the premises from the tenant, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant. Where deductions are made, an itemized statement shall be provided.

section.title: Eviction and recovery of possession of premises
section.text: (1) A landlord shall not be entitled to recover possession of any premises except on an application made by him to the Rent Court. (2) The Rent Court may make an order for the recovery of possession on grounds of non-payment of rent, denial of landlord's title, or misuse of premises after reasonable notice.

act.short_title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013

section.title: Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)
section.text: (1) Every employer of a workplace employing ten or more workers shall, by an order in writing, constitute a Committee to be known as the Internal Complaints Committee. (2) The Committee shall consist of: (a) a Presiding Officer who shall be a woman employed at a senior level; (b) not less than two Members from amongst employees preferably committed to the cause of women; (c) one member from amongst non-governmental organisations or associations committed to the cause of women. At least one-half of the total Members so nominated shall be women.

judgments.title: Aureliano Fernandes v. State of Goa and Others
judgments.ratio_decidendi: The Supreme Court issued nationwide directions emphasizing that serious lapses in constituting Internal Complaints Committees under Section 4 POSH Act render the entire disciplinary process unconstitutional, creating hostile environments for working women.

section.title: Payment of gratuity
section.text: (1) Gratuity shall be payable to an employee on the termination of his employment after he has rendered continuous service for not less than five years: (a) on his superannuation, or (b) on his retirement or resignation, or (c) on his death or disablement due to accident or disease. (2) For every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of six months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the rate of fifteen days wages based on the rate of wages last drawn. (6) The gratuity of an employee can only be forfeited to the extent of the damage or loss caused in case of termination for willful omission or negligence, or moral turpitude.
section.court_triable: Controlling Authority under Payment of Gratuity Act

judgments.title: Union Bank of India v. C.G. Ajay Babu
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Gratuity is a statutory right under Section 4 and cannot be withheld arbitrarily without conviction or proven quantification of moral turpitude.

section.title: Definitions (Consumer, Deficiency, Unfair Contract & Unfair Trade Practice)
section.text: (7) 'consumer' means any person who buys any goods or hires any service for a consideration. (11) 'deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance. (46) 'unfair contract' means a contract between a manufacturer/trader and a consumer having terms which cause significant change in rights of consumer including imposing unreasonable penalty or unilateral termination. (47) 'unfair trade practice' includes false representations and deceptive statements.

judgments.title: Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
judgments.ratio_decidendi: One-sided standard form contract terms constitute an unfair contract under Consumer Protection jurisprudence and are not binding upon consumers who have unequal bargaining power.

section.title: Liability of product manufacturer and e-commerce seller
section.text: (1) A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if: (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm.

act.short_title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

section.title: Application to Magistrate for emergency reliefs and protection
section.text: (1) An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act. (2) The relief sought may include protection orders (Section 18), residence orders in shared household (Section 19), monetary relief (Section 20), custody orders (Section 21), and compensation orders (Section 22). (4) The Magistrate shall fix the first date of hearing, which shall not ordinarily be beyond three days from the date of receipt of the application.
section.court_triable: Judicial Magistrate of the first class / Metropolitan Magistrate

judgments.title: Prabha Tyagi v. Kamlesh Devi
judgments.ratio_decidendi: Section 12 of the DV Act is a beneficial legislation; an aggrieved woman has an absolute right to reside in a shared household and petition for emergency protection regardless of whether she was cohabiting at the immediate time of complaint.
